notes: No trademarked fiction found in this batch (all real animals). Removed 'oldsquaw': the former name of the long-tailed duck, retired by the AOU as offensive; 'long-tailed duck' stays. Kept 'pacman frog' (real common name of Ceratophrys, though it derives from the game). Not separate: every species sub-theme reads as its parent (a deer, monkey, finch, owl or duck on a mammals/birds balloon is fine); colorful birds are all birds. Separate: bird body parts and birdwatching words are not birds. Accents follow Wikipedia/IOC usage (Grévy's zebra, Père David's deer, Rüppell's fox/vulture, Galápagos, Adélie penguin, Duméril's boa, Günther's dik-dik, vicuña, coquí); Maori names stay plain as in English dictionaries (kakapo, kaka, takahe, pukeko). Swapped text/uk to American-first for gray crowned crane and sulfur-crested cockatoo (both usually written grey/sulphur even in US sources; revert if you prefer the proper-name spelling). Added uk 'great grey owl'. No digit names apply to this batch (nine-banded, three-toed etc. are the standard spelled-out names). Most additions are fam 4-5 eponymous species ('X's ...') and three-plus-word names, zipf estimates 9-16. 'Christmas Bird Count' capitalised as a proper event name; 'Arctic' capitalised in species names.
